speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe your symptoms in detail. You mentioned double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; when did these symptoms first begin, and are they constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of diplopia triggered by looking up/down, proximal muscle weakness that worsens with activity (fatigability), and recovery with rest is highly characteristic of this autoimmune disorder.
